messages.subject: instantaneous speed and distance
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,
I am trying to estimate daily traveled distance using the code provided in the paper "Scale-insensitive estimation of speed and distance traveled from animal tracking data".

It has been working well until it got to the seventh day, since then it has been running with the status bar reaching 97% and going back to 45% for that day.

I have the instantaneous speed for this dataset, I got this fitting ctmm for the season, is there a way to estimate daily traveled distance from instantaneous speed?

All the best,

Adrian

messages.subject: Difference between isotropic and anisotropic
messages.body_plain:
Hey Chris,

So I have been working with your package and the results are really nice. We have gps tracking data of multiple individuals of bats and we have been able to create home ranges for each individual.

For each of these individuals, we always selected the best model, but sometimes an isotropic or an anisotropic model was chosen. It is for me not really clear what the difference is between an isotropic and an anisotropic model.

I read in the help file that isotropic or anisotropic determines whether the animal's covariance is circular or elliptical. For which data is isotropic the best method and when is anisotropic the best method. Furthermore, how does these two different methods affect the homerange, does it differ a lot between these two methods?

Thanks very much for your help,

Marinka

messages.subject: Re: instantaneous speed and distance
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

If the sampling distribution is heavy tailed, then you might get improvement in convergence by setting robust=TRUE, which will return the median of the sampling distribution rather than the mean.

You get distance traveled by estimating the mean speed and multiplying that by the time period.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Difference between isotropic and anisotropic
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marinka,

More elongated distributions will require anisotropic models to properly account for that in the KDE. Misapplying an isotropic model in this case would result in a biased estimate (too short along the long axis and too long along the short axis).
Relatively symmetric distributions will not support these extra parameters, and an isotropic model will be selected. Misapplying an anisotropic model in that case would result in extra statistical error from the unsupported parameters.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: re-orienting plots N-S while also using the 'move' package
messages.subject_clean: re-orienting plots N-S while also using the 'move' package
messages.body_plain:
I am brand new to ctmm and MoveBank.  I have run all example code in the ctmm.pdf user guide.  I have modified the orientation of the akde example plot to North-South.  Section 1 of the R code below runs and does that.

Next, in Section 2 below, I tried to reproduce that plot by reading an external CSV file and creating a telemetry object using the ‘move’ and ‘as.telemetry’ statements.  The ‘move’ statement is from the ‘move’ package.

The next line below used for re-orienting plots N-S results in an error apparently as a direct result of loading the ‘move’ package:

               projection(my.Telemetry) <- median(my.Telemetry)

 The error message is:

                Error in (function (cl, name, valueClass)  :

                  ‘crs’ is not a slot in class “telemetry”

               In addition: Warning message:

               In if (is.na <http://is.na>(x)) { :

                  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

That error even occurs in Section 1 if I simply load the ‘move’ package at the very top of the R code instead of waiting to load the ‘move’ package in Section 2.

The two plots appear to be largely the same other than the orientation.  The other major differences are the axes labels.  I will try to upload an image file containing the two plots.  I have not figured out how to modify the axes but will work on that next.

Here Chris recommends running external data through MoveBank.  I have not tried that yet.

                https://groups.google.com/u/4/g/ctmm-user/c/4_84SFHxSkE/m/BRv93FoYBgAJ

I have located the buffalo data set ‘Kruger African Buffalo, GPS tracking, South Africa.csv’ on MoveBank.  But I am not sure whether that will help if I still need to use the ‘move’ package with that data set.

Is there a way to re-orient plots N-S while using the ‘move’ package?

Thank you for any suggestions.

Here is the R code:

#

# Section 1

#

# Use just one buffalo, Cilla, and orient the plot north-south

# This section uses the built-in data and seems to work

library(ctmm)

library(suncalc)

data(buffalo)

Cilla <- buffalo$Cilla

write.csv(Cilla[, c("timestamp", "longitude", "latitude")],

     'Cilla_May22_2021.csv', row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

# annotate Cilla with sunlight data and compute colors

Cilla <- annotate(Cilla, cores=2)

# I do not know why there are two colors

COL <- color(Cilla, by='sun')

# use North-preserving projection and plot

projection(Cilla) <- median(Cilla)

plot(Cilla, col=COL)

compass()

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(Cilla, interactive=FALSE)

FIT <- ctmm.fit(Cilla, GUESS)

summary(FIT)

UD <- akde(Cilla, FIT)

plot(Cilla, UD=UD)

compass()

png(file="Cilla_plot1_May22_2021.png")

     plot(Cilla,UD=UD)

     compass()

dev.off()

###############

#

# Section 2

#

# This section uses an external CSV file and does not work

# The error seems to result from loading the 'move' package.

my.Data <- read.csv('Cilla_May22_2021.csv', header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

my.Data$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(my.Data$timestamp,format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz="UTC")

my.Data$`animal-ID` <- 'Cilla'

my.Data <- my.Data[order(my.Data$timestamp),]

head(my.Data)

library(move)

movedata <- move(x=my.Data$longitude, y=my.Data$latitude,

                 time=my.Data$timestamp,

                 data=my.Data,

                 # I do not know whether this proj is the same as with the built-in data

                 proj=sp::CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +ellps=WGS84"),

                 animal=my.Data$`animal-ID`)

# I do not know whether this proj is the same as with the built-in data

my.Telemetry <- as.telemetry(movedata, datum="WGS84")

summary(my.Telemetry)

my.Telemetry <- annotate(my.Telemetry, cores=2)

COL <- color(my.Telemetry, by='sun')

# The next statement returns an error because the move library was loaded

# The error occurs regardless of whether I use the built-in data or the external CSV file

projection(my.Telemetry) <- median(my.Telemetry)

projection(Cilla) <- median(Cilla)

# Error in (function (cl, name, valueClass)  :

#   ‘crs’ is not a slot in class “telemetry”

# In addition: Warning message:

# In if (is.na <http://is.na>(x)) { :

#   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

plot(my.Telemetry, col=COL)

compass()

my.GUESS <- ctmm.guess(my.Telemetry, interactive=FALSE)

my.FIT <- ctmm.fit(my.Telemetry, my.GUESS)

my.UD <- akde(my.Telemetry, my.FIT)

plot(my.Telemetry, UD=my.UD)

png(file="Cilla_plot2_May22_2021.png")

     plot(my.Telemetry, UD = my.UD)

dev.off()

png(file="Cilla_two_plots_May22_2021.png")

     par(mfrow=c(1,2))

     plot(Cilla,UD=UD) ; compass()

     plot(my.Telemetry, UD=my.UD) ; compass()

dev.off()

messages.subject_clean: re-orienting plots N-S while also using the 'move' package
messages.body_plain:
I think I have solved the problem by simply making sure the 'move' package is the first package I call.  In other words in the R code in my original post use:

                 library(move)
                 library(ctmm)

not:

                 library(ctmm)
                 library(move)

If I use:

                 library(ctmm)
                 library(move)

I get the following messages, indicating the 'projection' function from 'ctmm' is masked.

Loading required package: geosphere
Loading required package: sp
Loading required package: raster

Attaching package: ‘raster’

The following objects are masked from ‘package:ctmm’:

    distance, projection, projection<-

Loading required package: rgdal
rgdal: version: 1.5-23, (SVN revision 1121)
Geospatial Data Abstraction Library extensions to R successfully loaded
Loaded GDAL runtime: GDAL 3.2.1, released 2020/12/29
Path to GDAL shared files: C:/~/R/win-library/4.0/rgdal/gdal
GDAL binary built with GEOS: TRUE
Loaded PROJ runtime: Rel. 7.2.1, January 1st, 2021, [PJ_VERSION: 721]
Path to PROJ shared files: C:/~/R/win-library/4.0/rgdal/proj
PROJ CDN enabled: FALSE
Linking to sp version:1.4-5
To mute warnings of possible GDAL/OSR exportToProj4() degradation,
use options("rgdal_show_exportToProj4_warnings"="none") before loading rgdal.
Overwritten PROJ_LIB was C:/~/R/win-library/4.0/rgdal/proj

Attaching package: ‘move’

The following object is masked from ‘package:ctmm’:

    speed

>

If I use:

library(move)
library(ctmm)

and make no other changes to the R code in my original post then I get the plots I was expecting and are shown in the attachment.  I have always known there was the potential for problems if one package masked part of another.  But this is the first time I have ever encountered a serious issue resulting from masking.  Sorry I did not figure out this solution earlier.

Mark

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Sometimes functions from other packages are defined in a way that I can extend them with my own object classes, but I don't think this is the case with raster::projection(), at least the last time I checked. Instead of defining a generic that I can import, and dispatch methods for my object classes, they define a function that applies to every class.

What usually works no matter the order the packages are loaded in is to specify the package to be used like ctmm:::projection(), but sometimes R's dispatch routine will ignore that as well.

The safest method is to not load packages if you are just using a function or two from that package, but instead to call their functions like package::function().

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: trouble interpreting model fit with different error models
messages.subject_clean: trouble interpreting model fit with different error models
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I'm continuing my quest to deal with my extreme, multi-path errors in data from bighorn sheep collars. It's beyond my capabilities to use something like template model builder to implement a heavy-tailed error distribution, so I tried a different approach. Using stationary data, I built an external error model that predicts the position error in meters because it allowed for a little more flexibility/complexity in the model structure. I've tried to use these predictions in two ways ...

1) I assigned the predicted error to the HDOP column in the stationary data and use uere.fit to estimate how this relates to error - expecting the result to be near 1. The UERE estimate was 1.29 and when compared to any error model I've tried to fit with ctmm in the past, it is far superior, with a Z^2 of 1.9. Anything else I've tried with the same data would only get down to a Z^sq of about 5-6, unless I removed a lot of outlier data. I then assigned this UERE to my bighorn collar data and ran ctmm.fit. This resulted in much larger VAR.xy values than approach #2...

2) I also assigned the predicted error directly to the VAR.xy column of bighorn data, and ran ctmm.fit using this as the error model.

Points with error from approach 1 on the left, approach 2 on the right for one bighorn

I took one of the collars with the worst error in the data, and compared a no error model to models created from the above approaches. I looked at the semivariograms, the AIC values, and the predicted paths conditioned on the data. The AIC values suggest that the first approach, using the UERE with the predicted errors as the HDOP was a better fit, and the predicted locations are doing what I hoped - pulling in irregular "spikes" and predicting locations that are more reasonable given how I expect bighorn to move through these areas. This model also suggests that there is more autocorrelation in velocity than the other two models, which is what I would expect from bighorn movement. The semivariogram though, looks crazy and I'm not sure what's going on there or what this indicates. I wonder what you make of this...I can send you the data and code that I used to get to this point if you'd be willing to take a closer look.

Many thanks,
Christina

messages.body_plain:
Hi Christina,

I first need to know what your "predicted error" (pred.error) is supposed to correspond to. Is pred.error=VAR[x]=VAR[y] or is pred.error=SD[x]=SD[y] or something proportional to one of those? From the range of values, I'm guessing that it's supposed to be a variance in square meters?

Assuming that its supposed to be VAR[x] & VAR[y], then you would want to do something like

data$HDOP <- sqrt(2 * data$pred.error)
uere(data) <- 1 # you can possibly improve this with uere.fit() but I don't really know where these values come from to say

You should then have a VAR.xy column that is equal to your pred.error column (and with other variables set correctly in the latest versions of the package).
I checked and this has a reasonable looking plot and reasonable looking fit. There was no velocity autocorrelation selected for me with the RMS UERE set to 1, but I also didn't see any hint of that in the variogram even with error=TRUE.

I would try to stick to doing any error model selection on the calibration data, before working with the tracking data. There are known identifiability issues with the simultaneous estimation of error & movement parameters and I have also seen similar weirdness with simultaneous model selection on the error & movement models.

Best,
Chris
